message:
fix(host): sender permission point before the first datagram; secure input through one dispatch path with a versioned capture snapshot

Review conditions on 927b9f4 / 6a9aa32.

Sender (P11): the epoch is judged right before the first datagram, after pacing, and with
the fence active only an AU of the CURRENT epoch is sent -- old, untagged and future epochs
are dropped; untagged items pass only while the fence is inactive. The exception is stated
exactly: one AU per flush whose first datagram was permitted before the flush completes
with the metadata it was encoded with. Tests on the real sender thread: queued old AUs,
in-flight AU completes, and the new case -- held between the dequeue check and the first
datagram while the flush lands -> not one datagram; the IDR is next.

Secure input (P9): the capture target is one versioned record (window mode, HMONITOR,
stream generation) under a lock; secure_dispatch reads it, queries the monitor live,
re-checks the version, and stamps the verified rect into the message written under the
broker's lock (SendInputEventWithRect / SendInputTextWithRect). The secure branch, the
cached-default re-probe, the default-desktop broker fallback and the text path all go
through it -- the two paths that still called the broker directly could have revived the
agent's virtual-screen fallback. Unknown monitor, failed or empty query, window mode and a
target that changed during the query refuse the event. Tested with fake ports: first click
after an origin change carries the new rect; refusals send nothing; a broker write failure
is reported as such.

End to end: recovery S15 routes the fake host's AUs through the PRODUCT sender thread; an
AU held at the permission point plus queued ones behind it never start after the flush,
an in-flight one completes, the IDR follows, and the viewer stays Normal with no request.
